title: Triage result (base)
description:
What a router hands to whoever runs next. agents-md-schema.md rule 13.

BASE: `task_class` and `primary_agent` are left open and narrowed by the composing repository — a kernel router classifies contract and performance work, a docs router classifies records and narrative, and neither vocabulary belongs to the other. Two conventions the base does fix: `MULTI_DOMAIN` means no single class dominates, and a repository's `primary_agent` enum includes its own router, so re-entry is expressed rather than left implicit.

This file carries no `$id`: the bundle is vendored and every `$ref` into it is a relative path, so it resolves from the filesystem — on github.com, in CI without a network, and in a fresh clone alike. An `$id` would make the canonical identifier a URL that must then be fetched or registered.

task_class.description: The kind of work, decided before the route. SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; narrowed to the repository's enum.

primary_risk.description: One sentence: what goes wrong if this is routed badly. Not a restatement of the task.

primary_agent.description: The role that runs. Narrowed to the repository's enum, which includes its router.

execution_plan.description: Ordered steps. Lightweight by default: sequence, handoffs, gates.

validation_gates.description: Objects, not strings: the triage rule is that no gate is named without the risk it retires.

document_shape.description: Set when the task was a document-shape question. The vocabulary is ecosystem-wide (ADR-085 §G, and the three templates that are not interchangeable), so it is fixed here rather than per repository.

template_path.description: The template the shape selects, repository-relative. The layout differs per repository, so the pattern is narrowed by the composing schema.

next_action.description: The single best immediate move. One action, not a plan.

allOf.description: A shape decision that names ADR, RFC or RESEARCH names the template it selects.
